articles.title: 完形填空 · 在社交不足与社交透支之间找到平衡
articles.context: 文章讨论社交生活的适度原则：独处过多会带来孤独与脱节，社交过度又可能造成倦怠；更健康的做法是在恢复社交联系的同时，为自己明确留出不社交的休息时间。
rows: Your social life is defined as “the activities you do with other people, for pleasure, when you are not working”.
社交生活被定义为“你在不工作时，为了愉悦而与他人一起进行的活动”。
advance
It’s important to have a social life, but what’s right for one person won’t be right for another.
拥有社交生活很重要，但适合一个人的方式未必适合另一个人。
contrast
Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, whereas some of us may feel drained, even if it’s doing something we enjoy.
有些人与他人长时间相处会感到精力充沛，而另一些人即使参加自己喜欢的活动，也可能因此感到疲惫。
compare
This is why finding a balance in your social life is key.
因此，在社交生活中找到平衡至关重要。
emphasize
Spending too much time on your own, not seeing others, can make you feel lonely and disconnected.
独处太久、很少与人见面，会让你感到孤独，并与他人失去连接。
warning
Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and contribute to a low mood.
众所周知，孤独会影响心理健康，并使情绪低落。
explain
Anyone can feel lonely at any time.
任何人都可能在任何时候感到孤独。
qualify
This might be especially true if, for example, you are working from home and you are missing out on the usual social conversations that happen in an office.
例如，如果你居家办公，错过了办公室里日常发生的社交交谈，这种孤独感可能尤其明显。
example
Other life changes can trigger periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.
退休、换工作或成为父母等其他人生变化，也可能引发一段时期的孤独。
explain
It’s important to recognise these feelings of loneliness.
意识到这些孤独感很重要。
emphasize
There are ways to regain a social life, but it can feel overwhelming at first.
重新建立社交生活是有办法的，只是一开始可能让人觉得无从下手。
contrast
It’s a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy.
不妨先从想一想自己喜欢的爱好开始。
encourage
You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet like-minded people.
随后可以寻找与这些爱好相关的团体和活动，在那里结识志趣相投的人。
sequence
There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to try a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and share ideas.
有些团体面向新手父母，有些面向第一次想尝试某项新运动的人；同一职业的人也可以参加交流活动，见面分享想法。
example
On the other hand, it’s also possible to have too much of a social life.
另一方面，社交生活也可能过量。
contrast
If you feel like you’re always doing something and there is never any space in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social fatigue.
如果你总觉得自己一直在忙各种活动，日程表里从来没有留给放松的空档，就可能出现社交倦怠或社交疲劳。
warning
We all have our own social limit and it’s important to recognise when you’re feeling like it’s all too much.
每个人都有自己的社交上限；当你觉得这一切已经过量时，意识到这一点很重要。
emphasize
Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be signs of poor social health.
情绪低落、精力不足、易怒和睡眠困难，都可能是社交健康不佳的迹象。
warning
Make sure you mark out some time in your diary when you’re unavailable for socialising and use this time to relax, rest and recover.
务必在日程中明确划出一段“不参加社交”的时间，用来放松、休息和恢复。
encourage

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · AI 的收益若分配不均，技术扩散本身也会受阻
articles.context: Diane Coyle 认为，数字经济和 AI 要真正推动广泛繁荣，收益必须更均衡地分享；技术与财富过度集中在少数城市，会加剧不满并阻碍 AI 在地区经济中的应用，因此需要更公共、更地方化的技术想象。
rows: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress.
剑桥大学经济学家黛安·科伊尔在新书《齿轮与怪兽：经济学是什么，以及它应该是什么》中提出，数字经济要求我们以新的方式思考“进步”。
advance
“Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past,” she writes.
她写道：“无论我们所说的经济增长、情况变好究竟意味着什么，其收益都必须比近些年更均衡地得到分享。”
dialogue
“An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable.”
“如果一个经济体一边是科技百万富翁、亿万富翁和零工劳动者，一边是中等收入岗位被自动化侵蚀，那么它在政治上将难以持续。”
warning

Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle.
科伊尔说，要提高生活水平、让更多人更加繁荣，就需要更广泛地运用数字技术，提高医疗、建筑等各行业的生产率。
explain
But people can’t be expected to embrace the changes if they’re not seeing the benefits—if they’re just seeing good jobs being destroyed.
但如果人们看不到这些变化带来的好处，只看到优质工作岗位遭到破坏，就不能指望他们欣然接受变化。
contrast
In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech’s inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI.
科伊尔在最近一次采访中表示，她担心科技行业的不平等问题可能成为部署人工智能的障碍。
report
“We’re talking about disruption,” she says.
她说：“我们谈的是颠覆性变化。”
dialogue
“These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed.”
“这些都是变革性技术，会改变我们每天使用时间的方式，也会改变哪些商业模式能够成功。”
dialogue
To make such “tremendous changes,” she adds, you need social buy-in.
她补充说，要实现这种“巨大的变化”，就需要社会认同与支持。
emphasize
Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.
然而科伊尔指出，许多人认为收益流向了少数繁荣城市中的精英，因此不满情绪正在暗中积聚。
contrast
According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019.
布鲁金斯学会数据显示，到2019年，包括旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿和西雅图在内的仅八座美国城市，就拥有全国约38%的科技岗位。
statistic
New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings’s Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States.
新的人工智能技术更为集中：布鲁金斯学会的马克·穆罗和刘思凡估计，仅15座城市就占据了美国三分之二的人工智能资产与能力。
statistic
The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar.
少数城市主导人工智能的发明与商业化，意味着地域之间的财富差距还会继续扩大。
explain
Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.
正如科伊尔所说，这不仅会滋生政治和社会动荡，还可能阻碍地区经济增长所需要的那类人工智能技术。
warning
Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda.
解决办法的一部分，或许在于设法削弱大型科技公司对人工智能议程定义权的牢牢控制。
advance
That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants.
这很可能需要联邦政府增加对独立于科技巨头的研究的资助。
explain

A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don’t simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.
更直接的应对方式，是拓宽我们对数字技术的想象：设想那些不只是取代工作，而能在美国不同地区最关心的医疗、教育、制造业等领域扩大机会的人工智能技术。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 英国未来建筑木材危机与生产性植树不足
articles.context: 英国林业与木材行业组织 Confor 警告，长期未充分投资本土生产性林业，使英国高度依赖进口木材；面对建筑和净零需求，政府现有植树激励还不足以保证未来稳定木材供应。
rows: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned.
Confor 警告称，由于没有种植足够的产材林，英国未来将面临建筑业危机。
advance
The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country’s reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations.
这一林业和木材行业组织呼吁立即采取行动，减少英国对进口木材的依赖，并为后代提供稳定的木材供应。
explain
Currently only 20 per cent of the UK’s wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.
目前英国所需木材中只有20%产自国内，而英国仍是世界第二大木材净进口国。
statistic

Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don’t go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies.
英国政府近期出台新的激励措施，鼓励土地所有者多种树；但该行业组织认为这些措施力度不够，也没有充分宣传通过植树增加木材供应的好处。
contrast

“Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood,” said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor.
Confor 首席执行官斯图尔特·古德尔说：“我们现在不仅面临碳危机，而且由于没有为生产木材而植树，未来还会面临建筑业危机。”
dialogue

“For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall.”
“几十年来，我们一直没有承担起投资本国木材供应的责任，这使我们暴露在价格波动之下；随着全球需求上升而国内供应下降，我们还将不得不争夺未来的木材供应。”
dialogue
The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says.
Confor 表示，英国拥有种植建筑用木材、建设低碳住宅的理想条件，而且在森林可持续经营认证方面处于全球领先地位。
report
While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 per cent.
苏格兰约四分之三的住宅使用苏格兰木材建造，而英格兰使用本土木材的比例只有约25%。
compare
The causes of the UK’s current position are complex and range from outdated perceptions of productive forestry to the decimation of trees by grey squirrels.
英国之所以陷入当前局面，原因十分复杂，从对生产性林业的过时看法，到灰松鼠对树木的大规模破坏，都在其中。
explain
It also encompasses significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in longer-term planting projects.
其中还包括农民和其他土地所有者对投资长期植树项目的明显犹豫。
explain

While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK’s net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity.
尽管生产性植树能给农村经济带来实际的经济收益，并有助于英国的净零战略，但政府支持的重点仍放在粮食生产，以及单纯为保护生物多样性而进行的本土林地再野化和植树上。
contrast

Goodall added: “While food production and biodiversity health are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero.
古德尔补充说：“粮食生产和生物多样性健康当然极其重要，但我们的土地还需要为建筑业、制造业提供可靠的木材供应，并为实现净零目标作出贡献。
dialogue
“While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground.
“尽管英国政府已经表达了增加植树的雄心，但实际行动寥寥。
dialogue
Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand.”
Confor 现在呼吁为这些目标注入更强的推动力，以确保我们拥有足够的木材满足不断增长的需求。”
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 老年驾驶安全不能只靠劝退，更需要系统证据与适老汽车
articles.context: 文章讨论高龄驾驶者安全管理：停止驾驶对个人生活影响巨大，各州医生报告规则不一，相关研究又分散在多个专业；面对百岁寿命社会，还需要更好的证据、现场换证与视力检测，以及真正适合高龄驾驶者的汽车。
rows: One of the biggest challenges in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it’s time to turn over the keys.
让存在安全风险的高龄驾驶者离开道路，最大的难题之一，是说服他们到了交出车钥匙的时候。
advance
“It’s a complete life-changer” when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke.
前风险经理安妮·M·门克说，一个人停止驾驶——或者被迫停止驾驶——“会彻底改变他的生活”。
evaluation_quote

“The American Medical Association advises physicians that ‘in situations where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician’s advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles,’” Menke wrote.
门克写道：“美国医学会建议医生，‘如果有明确证据表明严重的驾驶能力受损会对患者本人和公共安全构成重大威胁，而且患者无视医生停止驾驶的建议，那么通知机动车管理部门是合适且符合伦理的。’”
dialogue
“Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality.
“有些州要求医生报告，有些州允许但不强制报告，还有少数州认为报告会违反保密义务。
dialogue
There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality,” she counseled.
她提醒说，如果医生没有依照州法律处理报告和保密问题，可能要承担法律责任并受到处罚。”
warning

Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan.
老年学家伊丽莎白·杜根说，保障高龄驾驶者安全的部分难题在于，这些问题被不同专业以各自不同的重点零散处理，包括老年学家、公路管理官员、汽车工程师等。
explain
“There’s not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies,” she said.
她说：“我们并没有一个‘国家老年驾驶研究所’。”
dialogue
“We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe” and what can help, said Dugan.
杜根说：“我们需要更好的证据来说明什么会使驾驶者变得不安全”，以及什么办法能够真正起作用。
emphasize
One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal.
一项看起来确实有效的措施，是要求驾驶者本人到场办理驾照续期。
advance
Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 per cent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study.
一项研究显示，强制本人到场续照与85岁及以上驾驶者致命事故减少31%相关。
statistic
Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.
通过视力测试也使这类驾驶者的致命事故出现相近幅度的下降，不过把两项措施结合起来似乎没有额外收益。
qualify
Many older drivers don’t see eye doctors or can’t afford to.
许多高龄驾驶者不去看眼科医生，或者负担不起相关费用。
report

Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can’t turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven’t changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily.
基层医疗人员本就十分忙碌，可能无法持续跟进那些因无法转头、记不清目的地而驾驶困难的患者；还有些人随着身高变矮，却没有相应调整座椅，以至于难以轻松踩到踏板。
explain
As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won’t solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan.
杜根说，只要道路上还有其他汽车，自动驾驶汽车就无法解决碰撞事故问题。
qualify
Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said.
她说，要避开所有人类驾驶者带来的危险，需要数量过于庞大的算法。
explain
But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan.
但杜根认为，我们仍需要做更多事情来提升安全。
contrast
“If we’re going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably.”
“如果人类将拥有百岁人生，我们就需要让90岁老人也能舒适驾驶的汽车。”
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 健康 App 的数据正在跑到既有隐私法律保护范围之外
articles.context: 健康应用迅速普及，但其收集的消费者健康数据常不受传统医疗隐私法同等保护；美国联邦贸易委员会主要只能事后执法，因此部分州开始通过自己的消费者数据隐私立法填补空白。
rows: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several.
如果看看手机里的应用，你很可能至少有一个与健康相关——而且多半不止一个。
advance

Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form.
无论是心理健康应用、健身追踪器、联网健康设备还是其他工具，我们中的许多人都在借助这类技术，以某种方式更好地追踪自己的健康状况。
explain
Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.
“护理与健康应用评审组织”的最新研究发现，市场上已有35万个健康应用，仅2020年就上线了9万个。
statistic
While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online.
尽管这些应用能提供很多帮助，但我们输入的个人信息究竟如何被收集、保护并在网上共享，并不总是清楚。
contrast

Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors’ offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online.
现有的健康隐私法律，例如《健康保险流通与责任法案》，主要关注医院、医生诊所、医疗机构和保险公司如何在线存储健康记录。
explain
The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.
而这些应用和健康数据追踪可穿戴设备所收集的健康信息，通常得不到同等程度的法律保护。
emphasize
Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated.
如果没有额外保护，公司可能会以消费者并未授权或预料的方式共享个人健康信息，甚至借此获利。
warning
In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation.
2021年，Flo Health 接受了美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的调查。
report
The FTC alleged in a complaint that “despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users’ sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties.”
FTC 在诉状中指称，“尽管公司明确作出隐私承诺，它仍掌控了用户敏感的生育数据，并将其分享给第三方。”
evaluation_quote

Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users’ express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.
Flo Health 与 FTC 通过一项同意令解决了此事：公司在共享应用用户的健康信息前，必须获得用户明确的肯定同意，并要求第三方删除此前取得的数据。
sequence

Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company’s privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm.
《联邦贸易委员会法》第5条授权 FTC 对不公平或欺骗性行为采取执法行动，这意味着只有当公司的隐私做法具有误导性或造成不正当的消费者损害后，FTC 才能事后介入。
explain

While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.
尽管 FTC 正尽力确保应用在处理敏感健康信息时兑现对消费者的承诺，但健康应用涌入市场的速度表明，这项挑战规模极其巨大。
contrast
As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term.
至于联邦立法前景，评论人士认为，短期内出台全面的联邦隐私立法似乎不太可能。
qualify
States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data.
各州已经开始实施自己的方案，以加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。
advance
California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018.
加利福尼亚州凭借2018年《加州消费者隐私法案》一直走在州级隐私保护行动的前列。
example
Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
弗吉尼亚州、科罗拉多州和犹他州近期也通过了州级消费者数据隐私立法。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 申请大学时，课外活动重在深度、独特性与真实影响
articles.context: 多位美国升学顾问指出，大学申请中的课外活动并非越多越好；真正有区分度的是持续投入、在常见活动中做到突出、开展独立项目、与未来专业相关，以及对社区产生真实积极影响。
rows: High school students eager to stand out in the college application process often participate in a litany of extracurricular activities hoping to bolster their chances of admission to a selective undergraduate institution.
为了在大学申请中脱颖而出，高中生常参加一长串课外活动，希望提高被选择性较强的本科院校录取的机会。
advance
However, college admissions experts say that the quality of a college hopeful’s extracurricular activities matters more than the number of activities he or she participates in.
然而大学招生专家表示，对申请者而言，课外活动的质量比参加活动的数量更重要。
contrast

Sue Rexford, the director of college guidance at the Charles E. Smith Jewish Day School, says it is not necessary for a student filling out the Common Application to list 10 activities in the application.
查尔斯·E·史密斯犹太日校大学升学指导主任苏·雷克斯福德说，学生填写 Common Application 时没有必要在申请表中列满10项活动。
report
“No college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list of extracurriculars that they have been passionately involved in each for an extended period of time,” Rexford wrote in an email.
雷克斯福德在邮件中写道：“没有哪所大学会期待一个学生列出一长串课外活动，而且每一项都长期、热情地投入其中。”
dialogue
Experts say it is tougher to distinguish oneself in a school-affiliated extracurricular activity that is common among high school students than it is to stand out while doing an uncommon activity.
专家表示，在高中生普遍参加的校内课外活动中脱颖而出，比通过一项少见的活动形成区分度更难。
compare

“The competition to stand out and make an impact is going to be much stiffer, and so if they’re going to do a popular activity, I’d say, be the best at it,” says Sara Harberson, a college admissions consultant.
大学招生顾问萨拉·哈伯森说：“想脱颖而出并产生影响，竞争会激烈得多。因此，如果学生要参加一项热门活动，我会说，那就做到最好。”
dialogue
High school students who have an impressive personal project they are working on independently often impress colleges, experts say.
专家说，高中生如果独立开展一项令人印象深刻的个人项目，往往能够打动大学。
report

“For example, a student with an interest in entrepreneurship could demonstrate skill and potential by starting a profitable small business,” Olivia Valdes, the founder of Zen Admissions consulting firm, wrote in an email.
Zen Admissions 咨询公司创始人奥利维娅·瓦尔德斯在邮件中写道：“例如，对创业感兴趣的学生可以通过创办一家盈利的小企业来展示能力和潜力。”
dialogue

Joseph Adegboyega-Edun, a Maryland high school guidance counselor, says unconventional extracurricular activities can help students impress college admissions offices, assuming they demonstrated serious commitment.
马里兰州高中升学顾问约瑟夫·阿德格博耶加-埃敦说，如果学生表现出认真投入，非常规的课外活动能够帮助他们给大学招生办公室留下深刻印象。
report

“Again, since one of the big questions high school seniors must consider is ‘What makes you unique?,’ having an uncommon extracurricular activity vs. a conventional one is an advantage,” he wrote in an email.
他在邮件中写道：“归根结底，高中毕业班学生必须思考的一个大问题是‘是什么让你与众不同？’因此，相比常规活动，拥有一项不常见的课外活动是一种优势。”
dialogue
Experts say demonstrating talent in at least one extracurricular activity can help in the college admissions process, especially at top-tier undergraduate institutions.
专家表示，至少在一项课外活动中展现出才能，会有助于大学申请，尤其是在顶尖本科院校的申请中。
emphasize

“Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive in the admissions process, especially for highly selective institutions, where having top grades and test scores is not enough,” Katie Kelley, admissions counselor at IvyWise admissions consultancy, wrote in an email.
IvyWise 招生咨询公司的顾问凯蒂·凯利在邮件中写道：“在某一种专注的课外活动中使自己脱颖而出，会成为申请中的加分项，尤其对高度选择性的院校而言，因为在那里仅有顶尖成绩和考试分数并不够。”
dialogue
“Students need to have that quality or hook that will appeal to admissions officers and allow them to visualize how the student might come and enrich their campus community.”
“学生需要具备某种能吸引招生官的特质或亮点，让招生官能够想象这个学生来到校园后会怎样丰富校园共同体。”
dialogue
Extracurricular activities related to the college major declared on a college application are beneficial, experts suggest.
专家指出，与大学申请中所申报专业相关的课外活动是有益的。
advance

“If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus,” says Mayghin Levine, the manager of educational opportunities with The Cabbage Patch Settlement House, a Louisville, Kentucky, nonprofit community center.
肯塔基州路易斯维尔非营利社区中心 The Cabbage Patch Settlement House 的教育机会经理梅金·莱文说：“如果你已经知道自己要读什么专业，有一项与该专业契合的课外活动会是很大的加分项。”
dialogue

High school students who have had a strong positive influence on their community through an extracurricular activity may impress a college and win a scholarship, says Erica Gwyn, a former math and science magnet program assistant at a public high school who is now executive director of the Kaleidoscope Careers Academy in Atlanta, a nonprofit organization.
埃丽卡·格温说，通过课外活动对所在社区产生强烈积极影响的高中生，可能会打动大学并赢得奖学金；她曾在一所公立高中担任数学与科学磁校项目助理，现任亚特兰大非营利机构 Kaleidoscope Careers Academy 执行主任。
conclude

articles.title: 翻译 · 农贸市场如何同时连接感官、生产者、本地经济与时令食物
articles.context: 文章描写农贸市场的感官体验与经济机制：消费者不仅能购买新鲜时令农产品并直接认识生产者，生产者也因减少中间商而获得更多利润，市场的规模和供给则随当地农业季节变化。
rows: With the smell of coffee and fresh bread floating in the air, stalls bursting with colourful vegetables and tempting cheeses, and the buzz of friendly chats, farmers’ markets are a feast for the senses.
空气里飘着咖啡与新鲜面包的香气，摊位上堆满色彩鲜艳的蔬菜和诱人的奶酪，耳边又是友好交谈的嗡嗡声，农贸市场堪称一场感官盛宴。
story
They also provide an opportunity to talk to the people responsible for growing or raising your food, support your local economy and pick up fresh seasonal produce—all at the same time.
它还让你能够与种植或饲养这些食物的人交谈，支持本地经济，同时买到新鲜的时令农产品——几件事一次完成。
advance
Farmers’ markets are usually weekly or monthly events, most often with outdoor stalls, which allow farmers or producers to sell their food directly to customers.
农贸市场通常每周或每月举办一次，多数设有露天摊位，让农民或生产者能够直接把食品卖给顾客。
explain
The size or regularity of markets can vary from season to season, depending on the area’s agricultural calendar, and you’re likely to find different produce on sale at different times of the year.
市场的规模或举办频率会随季节变化，这取决于当地的农业生产周期；一年中的不同时段，你往往会看到不同的农产品上市。
explain
By cutting out the middlemen, the farmers secure more profit for their produce.
通过省去中间商，农民能从自己的农产品中获得更多利润。
conclude
Shoppers also benefit from seeing exactly where—and to who—their money is going.
购物者也能从中受益，因为他们可以清楚看到自己的钱究竟流向哪里、又付给了谁。
conclude
